edits.original: Access checks default to fail-closed, rather than open.
edits.reason: Flagging for discussion: the trailer's contrast term is 'open' rather than the domain-standard antonym 'fail-open,' so I'm unsure whether the fail-closed/fail-open default distinction counts as ordinary general knowledge (cut the trailer) or a genuine, checkable distinction (give it its own sentence); I don't want to silently cut or rewrite it.

edits.original: Those privilege limits are imposed on purpose, rather than by accident.
edits.replacement: Those privilege limits are imposed on purpose.
edits.reason: 'By accident' is the ordinary-knowledge antonym of 'on purpose' (the rule's own WRONG example), so the tacked-on 'rather than by accident' trailer adds nothing and is cut.
